title: GTA VI: The Album Spins Through Jazz, Hip-Hop, Pop, and More
summary:
Grand Theft Auto VI took 13 years to make, and its music is just as big an event as the game. The album Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album works like a radio dial, flipping fast between wildly different styles — smooth jazz, hip-hop, pop, country, and blues.

The opening track, 'Starting From Zero,' pairs the electronic duo Justice, who composed the game's score, with soul singer Michael McDonald. Thudding synths and McDonald's instantly recognizable voice give it the feel of a classic buddy-cop movie theme. The closing track, 'Overtown Lights,' brings together bassist Stanley Clarke, pianist Robert Glasper, and drummer Yussef Dayes for a relaxed, late-night drive.

Other tracks jump straight into today's sounds. 'That's It' teams Swedish rapper Yung Lean with Atlanta rapper Future and producer Metro Boomin, mixing icy synths with trap beats and deep bass. Hip-hop stars Travis Scott, Playboi Carti, Cardi B, and Young Thug also appear, along with a high-energy Kodak Black and Don Toliver collaboration called 'Let's Rock.'

The album also celebrates Spanish-language music. Regional Mexican stars Fuerza Regida bring a thumping track called 'Suzuki,' while singer-songwriter Helado Negro and singer Kali Uchis team up on 'Largate,' a dreamy song about a breakup that the review calls one of the album's true highlights.

Pop moves fast here too. BLACKPINK's JENNIE rides robot-rocking synths on 'Power Trip,' Zara Larsson nods to fellow Swedes Ace of Base on 'Fast Emotion,' and Camila Cabello finds a middle ground between her speedy and mellow styles. Country star Morgan Wallen, blues legend Keith Richards, and funk producer Dam-Funk also appear.

With so many genres packed into one album, listening feels like spinning a radio dial and landing somewhere new every few minutes. That variety, the review says, makes it a snapshot of popular music right now.
why_it_matters: Music shapes how games feel, and an album that mixes many styles shows how different kinds of music can reach the same listeners.

background_read: A video game score is the music written to fit a game's story and scenes, so it can make a car chase feel tense or a quiet drive feel calm.
An album is a collection of songs released together, and artists often mix styles on one album to reach different listeners.
Hip-hop, jazz, pop, country, and blues are different styles of popular music, each with its own sound and history.
A review is a writer's opinion about a new album, game, or show, explaining what works and what does not.
